extracted.intended_audience: manuscript authors, especially early-career researchers preparing responses to journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting a professional, complete, point-by-point response letter to journal peer reviewers and for deciding/ documenting how to revise the manuscript (or politely disagree). Emphasizes structure, tone, documentation, and example phrasings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thank reviewers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you thank the journal referees and journal editor(s) for their time and insightful feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open your response with gratitude; this sets a professional tone. Anti-pattern: beginning defensively or omitting a simple thank-you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-by-point responses quoting each reviewer comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote each reviewer comment and draft a point-by-point response, leaving no room for error or accidental omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the response letter so every referee remark is reproduced verbatim (or clearly labeled) followed by the author's reply. This ensures nothing is overlooked and makes it easy for editors/reviewers to verify changes. Use consistent labeling (Reviewer 1, Comment 1.1, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert a summary of major changes at the top
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert an additional section at the top that briefly summarizes all major changes made to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise high-level changelog (e.g., new experiments, major rewrites, added analyses) so editors quickly see the scope of revisions without reading the full point-by-point list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise cross-references to manuscript locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you direct the reviewers to the appropriate page(s) and line number(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you state that you modified text or added results, cite exact page/line numbers, section names, figure/table numbers. This helps reviewers verify edits quickly. Example phrasing used in the article: 'The updated text can be found in [mention the section(s)].'

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnish appropriate references where required
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish all appropriate references wherever required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defending interpretations or adding background/context, cite relevant literature. If rejecting a suggested change on scientific grounds, support that stance with citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use formatting (e.g., color-coding) to differentiate elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use color-coding to differentiate between referee comments, your responses, and the changes made in the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual cues (colors, fonts, indentation) make long response documents easier to parse. Ensure any color use is accessible and compatible with journal submission systems; alternatively use clear labels if colors are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version your response/manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention the manuscript version (e.g., 'Revised Manuscript V2') in your response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate which version of the manuscript the responses refer to to avoid confusion if multiple revision rounds occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional, respectful language and avoid defensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective authors should maintain professional and respectful language in all communications with journal referees and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not respond in haste. Even when disagreeing, phrase responses politely and factually. Anti-patterns: accusatory language, ad hominem remarks, dismissing comments without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully analyze reviewer comments to understand intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligent researchers carefully analyze reviewer comments and strive to understand what other experts are trying to communicate; the idea is not to get defensive but to open your mind and listen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether reviewers identify missing controls, misinterpretations, or clarity issues. Treat comments as opportunities to improve scientific accuracy and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: If suggested experiments are outside scope, explain politely and strengthen argument alternatively
rubrics_metrics.description: If the journal reviewers suggest experiments that are way outside the scope of your research expertise, highlight this limitation clearly but politely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example Author Response #1: explain scope limits, state why the suggestion is not feasible (resources/time/expertise), and describe alternate steps taken (e.g., added analyses, cited literature, highlighted limitations). Offer openness to future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: If suggestions are logically flawed or inaccurate, consult peers then rebut with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In case you come across logically flawed or inaccurate suggestions, discuss them with your peers first. If they also agree with you, then explain your stance politely in your response letter and support it with the required scientific evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not simply reject a reviewer's point; show reasoning and cite data or references that justify maintaining your approach. Document the peer consultation if helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you accept requested experiments or analyses, document what was done and where
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe that the additional experiments are necessary and can be completed, conduct them and incorporate the results into the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example Author Response #2: describe the new experiments/analyses briefly, state where the new data are presented (sections, figures, tables), and confirm incorporation across relevant text to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise conclusions or clarify and add evidence when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Author Response options: revise conclusions if you agree they were inaccurate, or if you maintain interpretation, clarify reasoning and add supporting references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising, indicate exact changes and rationale. If retaining original interpretation, strengthen the argument with additional explanation/citations and show where changes were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Methods contain all key details for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to comments requesting missing key details in Materials and Methods by adding those details so other researchers can reproduce and build upon the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's quiz emphasizes selecting the option to add required key details (Answer C). Anti-patterns: justifying lack of detail or ignoring reproducibility concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use peers to vet disagreements and difficult responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss contentious or unclear reviewer suggestions with colleagues before drafting a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer input helps determine whether to accept, partially accept, or rebut a suggestion and provides evidence/support to include in the response letter.
